Heard SriArvind Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State,
Ms. Seema Kashyap, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

2. The present appeal has been filed under Section 14-A (2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 against the order dated 05.07.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act,
Pratapgarh in Bail Application No. 1593 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 0079 of 2024, under Sections- 147, 149, 323, 504, 365, 376(D) IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act, P.S.- Patti, District- Pratapgarh.

sentences.text: 4. It is further stated that prior to the FIR in issue registered as Case Crime No. 0079 of 2024 on 03.03.2024, indicating therein the date of incident as 25.02.2024, against the appellant and others under Sections 147, 149, 323, 504, 506, 365, 328, 376-D IPC and Sections 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Dha) and 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act at P.S.- Patti, District- Pratapgarh, the victim lodged the FIR No. 0438 dated 15.10.2023 against the one Krishna Kumar Yadav @ Pankaj making allegations therein so as to attract the offences as indicated under Sections 323, 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act and Section 67 of IT Act.

5. It is further stated that prior to the FIR lodged on 15.10.2023, indicated above, an FIR No.
297/2011 dated 13.07.2011 was also lodged by the husband of the victim/opposite party No. 2 at about 33.30 hours making allegations therein so as to attract the offences as indicated under Section 323, 452, 498, 336, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(10) of SC/ST Act.
6. It is further stated that from the aforesaid, it is apparent that only to get the pecuniary benefits from the State Exchequer, the FIRs have been lodged either by the victim or by her husband.
7. It is further stated that as per the case setup by the prosecution in the FIR in issue against the appellant and others, it is a case of gang rape.
However, the medical opinion does not support the case of prosecution, as according to the same, upon due medical examination, no injury was found by the concerned doctor over the body of victim.

8. It is also stated that the FIR, in issue, also says that the victim was abducted on 25.02.2024 while she was going to ease herself by the appellant and co-accused namely Ganesh Yadav, Ganesh Singh,
Amresh Yadav and 3-4 others.
However, according to the statement of victim recorded in terms of Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim was abducted while she was going at the residence of Bank Manager to cook food.
As such, the story of prosecution is doubtful.

9. It is lastly submitted that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the impugned order dated05.07.2024 is liable to be set-aside and the appellant, whois languishing in jail since 25.04.2024, is entitled to be released on bail.

10. Learned A.G.A. as also counsel for the opposite party No. 2 opposed the prayer of the appellant,
however, they could not dispute the above contentions made by the appellant's counsel particularly based upon the FIRs and the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
11.

Considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. and gone through the contents of the appeal, impugned order, F.I.R., as well as other relevant documents including the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
12.

Upon due consideration of above facts and circumstances including the story setup in the FIR and the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and the medical Kamlesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195348592/
2 examination of the victim and keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, this Court is of the view that the appeal has substance and it is accordingly, allowed.
13. Orderdated 05.07.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Pratapgarh in Bail Application No.
1593 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 0079 of 2024, under Sections- 147, 149, 323, 504, 365,
376(D) IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act, P.S.- Patti, District- Pratapgarh is hereby set aside.

sentences.text:
14. Let the appellant-Kamlesh Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions :-
(i) The appellant will cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
(iii) The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(es).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
15.
In case of default of above conditions it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

16. As this order relates to enlargement of the appellant on bail, it is clarified that observations made in this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and the trial court shall not be influenced by any observation made in this order.
